saa-med-325.text: A Bucket S3 build up application logs: the first 30 days are frequently consulted; up to 90 days, rarely; after that, almost never — but they need to be retained by 5 years for compliance, at the lowest cost. DUAS do actions optimize cost by complying with the requirement? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Create a lifecycle rule with transitions: Standard → Standard-IA to 30 days → S3 Glacier Deep Archive to 90 days
Delete the logs after 1 year to save
Configure the expiration of objects to 5 years (1.825 days) in the same lifecycle rule
Replicate logs to another region to reduce cost
Move everything immediately to One Zone-IA on upload
saa-med-325.explanation: A) Correct: the stepwise transition follows the access pattern — frequent (Standard), rare (IA), deep archiving (Deep Archive, the cheapest class). 5 (c) Correct: automatic expiry at the end of 5 years eliminate residual cost without manual process. D) Incorrect: replication DUPLICA (e) Incorrect: One Zone-IA has less resilience and minimal recovery of 30 days; does not meet the initial frequent access nor is it the cheapest class for the long term.

saa-med-326.text: A bank RDS MySQL suffers with slowness caused by (1) heavy reading reports carried out on business hours, and (2) identical repetitive consultations of a product catalogue. DUAS Do solutions attack each cause, respectively? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Enable Multi-AZ No RDS
Create Read Replicas and direct reports to them
Enable automatic backups with greater retention
Add Amazon ElastiCache to cache the repetitive queries from the catalog
Migratory to Aurora Serverless without other changes
saa-med-326.explanation: A) Incorrect: Multi-AZ is available (invisible standby), does not relieve reading. B) Correct: Read Replicas scale to LEITURA — the reports leave the primary. C) Incorrect: backups do not affect query performance. D) Correct: cache (ElasiCache Redis/Memcached) responds to repeated queries in memory, removing this bank load. E) Incorrect: change the capacity model does not solve the two identified causes by itself..

saa-med-327.text: Courts EC2 in private sub-networks (without NAT and without IGW) need access DOIS destinations without going through the internet: (1) Buckets S3 and (2) a API of the AWS Secrets Manager. Which ones DOIS types of VPC Should Endpoint be used, respectively? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Gateway Endpoint for the S3 (entry into the road table, free of charge)
Endpoint interface for the S3 mandatory
Gateway Endpoint for the Secrets Manager
Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) for the Secrets Manager, creating a ENI in the subnet
NAT Gateway for both
saa-med-327.explanation: A) Correction: S3 (and DynamoDB) support Gateway Endpoints — free, implemented as route on the road table. B) Incorrect: there is Interface Endpoint for S3, But it's not mandatory and cost-effective — Gateway is the default choice.: Secrets Manager DO NOT support Gateway Endpoint (only S3/DynamoDB D) Correct: for other services, the private path is the Interface Endpoint via PrivateLink (ENI in the sub-network).: NAT gives way to the INTERNET — violates the requirement and adds cost.

saa-med-328.text: A critical global application needs DR between regions with RPO close to zero in two layers: (1) PostgreSQL compatible relational bench and (2) Table NoSQL with reading and writing locals in each region. DUAS Do solutions respond, respectively? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: RDS PostgreSQL with daily snapshots copied between regions
Aurora Global Database, with replication between regions with typical lag lower than 1 second
DynamoDB with on-demand backups restored in the other region
DynamoDB Global Tables, with active multi-region replicas
ElestiCache Redis with weekly snapshot
saa-med-328.explanation: A) Incorrect: daily snapshots mean RPO up to 24 hours — far from zero. Aurora Global Database replicates for secondary regions with subsequent lag (RPO ~1(c) Incorrect: manual backup/restore has RPO/RTO D) Correct: Global Tables are active-active: reading and writing local in each region with automatic replication. E) Incorrect: cache with weekly snapshot is not primary data DR solution.

saa-med-329.text: After an incident, a company wants to strengthen the security of the account AWS: (1) prevent the unprotected use of the root user; and (2) register TODAS calls from API of all the organization's accounts for audit. DUAS do measures implement these points? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Share root credentials only with the security team
Enable MFA in root user and save your credentials for emergency use only
Create a billing alarm
Create an organization trail in AWS CloudTrail, applied to all accounts of the AWS Organizations
Enable Amazon Inspector in all accounts
saa-med-329.explanation: A) Incorrect: sharing root credentials increases risk — root should not be used on a daily basis. B) Correct: MFA in root + use restricted to emergencies is the fundamental practice of account protection. C) Incorrect: billing alarm monitors cost, non-security of API. D) Correct: the trail organization centralizes the register of TODAS calls from API of all the Member accounts — the basis of the audit.: Inspector varre vulnerabilities in workloads; does not record calls from API.

saa-med-330.text: A site served by the CloudFront of a kind used in S3 needs DUAS guarantees: (1) no one can access the objects by going directly to the URL of the Bucket, and (2) the content cannot be served for certain countries by legal restriction. DUAS settings answer? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Origin Access Control (OAC) no CloudFront + Bucket policy allowing only distribution
Make the public newsletter with reading policy
Sign all objects with presigned URLs from 7 days
Enable geographical restriction (geo restriction) of distribution CloudFront
Blocking countries with rules of Security Group no bucket
saa-med-330.explanation: A) Correct: OAC, the bucket is private and the bucket policy authorizes only the service CloudFront — direct access to S3 is denied. B) Incorrect: public newsletter is exactly what you want to prevent. C) Incorrect: presigned URLs give temporary access to point; it is not the mechanism to serve an entire site via CDN. D) Correct: the geo-restriction of CloudFront lock (or allows) specific countries on the edge.: Security Groups do not apply to pocketes S3.

saa-med-331.text: One API public Amazon API Gateway suffers from abusive customers and spikes that knock down the backend. (1) limit the rate of requests per identified customer; and (2) block malicious patterns and abusive IPs before they reach API. Which ones DUAS do measures implement this? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Increase Backend Integration Timeout
Configure usage plans with API keys and throttling limits per customer
Associate one AWS WAF at the stage of API, with managed rules and rate-based rules
Publish a API in multiple regions
Enable cache of responses in the stage
saa-med-331.explanation: A) Incorrect: more timeout only prolongs backend suffering under abuse. B) Correct: use plans + API keys apply fee and quota limits POR CLIENTE — the consumption control requested. C) Correct: o WAF in front of the API SQLi block/XSS, IPs and apply rate-based rules against flood, before backend. D) Incorrect: multi-region is availability/latence, not protection against abuse. E) Incorrect: cache helps performance of repeated readings, but does not limit customers or block attacks.

saa-med-332.text: A stream of the Kinesis Data Streams in Provisioned Mode presents ProvidedThroughputExceededException errors in producers at peak times, and the load is unpredictable. DUAS Do actions solve the problem? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: Migrate the stream to the on-demand capability mode, which automatically scales
Reduce the stream retention period to 12 hours
Do resharding (increase the number of shards) to increase the capacity of provided writing
Switch the partition key to a single constant to simplify
Add one DLQ to stream
saa-med-332.explanation: A) Correct: On-demand mode automatically dimension capacity according to traffic — ideal for unpredictable load. B) Incorrect: retention affects storage/replay, not write limit. C) Correct: in the provided mode, more shards = more capacity (1 MB/s or 1.000 D) Incorrect: constant key partition creates A hot shard — drastically worsens the problem. E) Incorrect: DLQ is the concept of rows/Lambda; does not increase stream throughput.

saa-med-333.text: A team wants to roll containers in AWS with the MENOR possible operational effort and cost proportional to use: without managing servers, without planning cluster capacity and paying for vCPU/memory consumed by tasks. DUAS characteristics AWS Fargate do they support that choice? (Select DUAS alternatives)
options: The Fargate eliminates instance management EC2 cluster — no hosts to provide, scale or apply patches
The Fargate requires the administration of a node group of EC2
The collection of Fargate is by resources (vCPU and memory) allocated to the tasks by the execution time
The Fargate is free for even workloads 4 vCPUs
The Fargate only works with Kubernetes
saa-med-333.explanation: A) Correct: no Fargate a AWS manage the entire execution infrastructure — the team only handles the task definitions. EC2 are the way EC2 of the ECS/EKS, exactly what the Fargate C) Correct: paid for vCPU/GB per second while the task runs — cost proportional to use. D) Incorrect: no free layer by task size. E) Incorrect: the Fargate executes both tasks of ECS how much pods of EKS.
